Subject: Benchmark sprint & MAP: Embeddings + Reranker performance validation

Ben —

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion, I want to lock down a short MAP and an evaluation plan we can run next week that validates AtlasDocs' production targets and gives us clear acceptance criteria for close. High-level asks from your side: target QPS, sample payload sizes (average token counts for documents and queries), and any traffic shape constraints (bursts vs steady).

Proposed test window: Apr 22–23 (US daytime). Proposed matrix (we can adjust after you share traffic):
- Embedding endpoint: concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16], batch sizes [8,32,64], warm-up 5m, steady 15m per point. Measure qps, p50/p95/p99, and TTFT (time-to-first-token).
- Reranker endpoint: rerank-batched and per-query modes. Test concurrency [1,2,4,8,16], candidate pool sizes [10,50,100], batch sizes [4,16]. Measure end-to-end latency, p95 for reranker-stage, and throughput (queries/sec).

Success criteria (proposal):
- Embeddings: steady p95 < 200ms at target steady QPS (you indicated ~200qps) and TTFT < 150ms.
- Reranker: steady p95 < 400ms at target QPS (you indicated ~40qps) for candidate pool 50.

Marissa (cc'd) will provide the test harness and exact config. If that looks good, can you send sample payloads and preferred run times? I'll draft a short MAP with milestones (SOW, run dates, sign-off).

Best,
Hannah

- Our steady target is 220 qps for embedding calls (mostly short docs, avg 128 tokens) and ~45 qps for reranker (candidate pool ~50, average query tokens ~16). Bursts up to 2.5x for short spikes.
- TTFT goal: sub-120ms ideal, acceptable up to 180ms for embeddings. Reranker TTFT target sub-200ms if possible.

I'm attaching a small sample of representative queries/documents and one internal run we did against a mock endpoint so you can see our payload distribution. We'll be available for the Apr 22–23 window — prefer mornings (PST).

Hi Ben —

Attaching the detailed bench plan and test configs. Key points and what we'll measure:

Test environment
- Hardware: 2x A100 (40GB) per node, 8 nodes isolated in our dedicated test pool.
- Models: redwood-emb-1.0 (fp16), redwood-rerank-0.9 (kv-cache enabled)
- Runtime: Redwood inference runtime with continuous batching and KV-prefix caching disabled for cold-start analysis; caching will be enabled in a separate run.

Measurement plan
- Metrics: TTFT (time from request to first token on stream), token latency, endpoint p50/p95/p99, throughput (queries/sec), GPU util, memory.
- Sweep axes: concurrency [1,4,8,16,32], batch sizes (embeddings) [8,32,64], batch sizes (reranker) [4,16,32], candidate sets [10,50,100].
- Run policy: 5m warm-up, 15m steady-state sampling per test point. Two repeats per point; collect median of runs.
- Failure criteria: any point where p95 > 2x target or p99 shows unbounded tails (consistent >1s) will be flagged and investigated.

Predicted acceptance bands (based on prior Redwood runs and your payload):
- Embeddings: expected steady throughput 220–300 qps at p95 <= 180–220ms for batch 32, TTFT expected ~90–130ms.
- Reranker (cand=50): expected 35–50 qps at p95 <= 300–420ms depending on batch; TTFT expected ~120–200ms.

Test artifacts we will produce:
- bench-plan-v1.pdf (high-level plan + config)
- test-config.yaml (exact locust/runner flags + payload paths)
- emb-rerank-results-summary.csv (aggregated metrics per sweep point)

Two notes:
1) We'll run a baseline with caching disabled to measure cold-start behavior and then a second pass with prefix/KV caching enabled (this often improves reranker tail).
2) If you have any hard SLAs or compliance windows, call those out before Apr 21 so we can include in MAP.

I'll schedule the harness to run Apr 22 at 09:00 PST. Confirm you can provide the sample payloads and we will upload aggregated CSVs to the shared Drive.

Marissa Cole
Principal Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Initial internal run results

Marissa/Hannah —

We ran a quick internal pass yesterday against a staging endpoint to validate harness compatibility. Summary highlights:
- Embedding endpoint (avg payload 128 tokens): steady 210 qps at p95 ~210ms, TTFT median 140ms. At concurrency 32 / batch 64 we saw p99 spikes up to ~950ms.
- Reranker (cand=50): steady 38 qps p95 ~360ms; p99 ~780ms at the highest concurrency points.

CSV attached: atlas-run1.csv. The tail behavior looks correlated with occasional CPU throttling on the staging host during spikes — working with our infra team to rule out any client-side artifact.

Ask: If Redwood can run the same matrix on your dedicated test pool (the one Marissa described), focus on two things: (1) reproduce the p99 tail for embeddings at high concurrency and (2) assess reranker improvements with caching enabled. We'll share the infra notes and a short replay script.

Ben
Benjamin Lowe
Head of Engineering, AtlasDocs

Thanks Ben — and thanks Marissa for the plan. Quick summary and proposed MAP / close timeline so we have alignment:

MAP milestones (proposed)
- Apr 22: Redwood runs full bench matrix (baseline caching OFF). Deliverables: emb-rerank-results-summary.csv, raw CSVs, Grafana dashboards.
- Apr 23: Redwood runs caching-enabled pass + targeted tuning (kernel/quantization knobs). Deliverables: tuned-results-summary.csv, ops notes.
- Apr 25: Joint review call to validate acceptance criteria and agree on next steps (SOW + pricing adjustments if required).
- May 3: Exec sign-off (AtlasDocs) — target close date for Dedicated capacity trial.

Acceptance criteria (final):
- Embeddings: p95 <= 220ms at 220 qps steady; TTFT <= 180ms.
- Reranker: p95 <= 400ms at 40 qps steady with candidate set 50.

Action items:
- Atlas: share final sample payloads + any infra constraints (by EOD Apr 19) — Ben noted this is done.
- Redwood (Marissa): run matrix Apr 22–23, upload CSVs and link to Drive.
- Hannah/Neha: prepare SOW draft and HubSpot update (deal ATL-2027-039).

If that aligns, we'll go ahead with the runs and meet Apr 25 for review. Thanks everyone — excited to close this out.
